title: Development of a Crystallographic Model of the Interface (CH3NH3Pb(I,Clx)3-x / TiO2) from HRTEM Images and the Effect the CL in the Electron Density Distribution of the Perovskite Solar Cells
content: An atomic model of the interface (CH3NH3Pb(I,Clx)3-x / TiO2) that composes up the n-i junction in hybrid perovskite solar cells was developed from HRTEM images. This model allowed the crystallographic interpretation of these materials and, although they are susceptible to degradation due to electron beam damage produced when they are under TEM observation, the TEM images do allow observation and structural study of Moire patterns, double diffraction, prohibited points, and dislocations in the [11¯2¯] zone axis. From the model developed, the computer simulation of the interface was performed, identifying the presence of Moire patterns generated by a 7.6° rotation angle between the two materials and the dislocations generated by the mismatch. Finally, theoretical calculations of the interface, such as Morse potential, PDOS, and the electronic density distribution, were carried out for the CH3NH3PbI3 / TiO2 and CH3NH3Pb(I,Clx)3-x / TiO2 interface, finding that the presence of chlorine promotes a greater electron density distribution [1].
